key_insight: DxToniaNet estimated expert-rated leg dystonia severity from clinical videos of children with cerebral palsy, with a reported mean absolute error of 1.71 points on a 0–40 scale.
clinical_relevance: Video-based severity estimation could support more consistent dystonia assessment in care and trials, but clinical utility requires further evaluation.
method: Used OpenPose to extract bilateral knee, ankle, and toe coordinates from seated hand open-close task videos.
Calculated 69 normalized movement variance and amplitude features.
Trained a neural network using five-fold cross-validation at Center 1, then tested it independently at Center 2.
evidence_signal: The retrospective dataset included videos from 298 children across two centers; among videos meeting the dystonia inclusion threshold, reported testing MAE was 1.71 points and accuracy was 90–94% for distinguishing video pairs differing by more than 4 GDRS points.
watch_item: Development and testing included only videos with expert-rated dystonia, so performance in children without dystonia and in prospective clinical workflows remains unestablished.
paper_title: DxToniaNet: A Neural Network for Estimating the Severity of Leg Dystonia in Children with Cerebral Palsy
